Polaniec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Połaniec, Poland

Demolished. Jews settled in Połaniec from the 16th century; by 1921, 980 (38%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in autumn 1942. This cemetery was established around 1647 under a royal grant from King Władysław IV Waza, with an additional 1765 guarantee from King Stanisław August Poniatowski confirming burial rights. During WWII, victims of the October 18-19, 1942 deportation to Staszów were executed and buried here; the last funeral likely occurred in spring 1945, following the murder of the Berger family. Poland's National Council formally moved to close the cemetery in 1957, followed by a 1964 ministerial order authorizing other uses for the land; a 1961 notice warned the Łódź Jewish congregation of plans to build an agronomic office and garages there.
